calibration_value: This transition is intentionally allowed to have a degenerate all-retired frontier. It tests that ReplayMark does not force reuse when a real API family has been retired.

claim_boundary.historical_action_reuse_means: delegate the exact historical HA service action; semantic substitution/regeneration is not ReplayMark reuse

expected_frontier_summary.reason: At the frozen native-service-call boundary both old operations differ from the New Direct operations; ReplayMark cannot call a semantically substituted operation and still call it reuse.

nonclaims: This frontier does not claim the old and new downstream temperature effects are always different.
This frontier does not treat migration to a new service as replay of the old service.
Current migration documentation may show effect-equivalent simple round trips; that is outside this exact historical-action reuse boundary.

service_effect_witness.restore: if saved temperature present, restore it, clear saved value, and enqueue control
service_effect_witness.set: if saved temperature absent, save current target; set target to requested temperature; enqueue control; subsequent set changes target without overwriting saved value

old_native_law.service_registration_witness: old services.yaml declares save/restore/set_temp_target_temperature and old climate.py registers set/restore entity services

state_space.completeness_argument: Both old and new blueprints use the same two state-change triggers and one binary state test; no third thermostat action path exists.
state_space.minimality_argument: The blueprint has exactly two reachable trigger-result branches under the fixed configuration: schedule on and schedule off. night_temp is configuration, not a dynamic state dimension, and is frozen at 18.0 C.
